correctness.rationale: General support criterion proved by single outside-vertex parity repair and worst-trace reduction; rank dichotomy proved by deleting one element of a maximum independent set and external-private-neighbor equivalence. Path upper bounds use maximum independent set uniqueness/spacings and all-positive/last-negative tree obstruction. Coupled endpoint Ldim lower recurrences attain the upper bound in all four residues. Exceptional n=1,2,4 individually verified. Independent Python full graph/path and C++ direct trace/rank computations check the claimed finite instances, but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: A general finite-graph support characterization and exact alpha-1/alpha rank criterion provide a reusable structural result. The all-n path theorem isolates an alternating mod-four parity effect and exactly one unit of online advantage on every even order n>=6, in contrast to equal static dimensions. The theorem concerns natural weight-parity constrained independent-set languages and is not a single small isolated computation.
